newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam denies Algerian coffee shipment cancelled.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam denies Algerian coffee shipment cancelled.

text.p: Vietnam's state coffee company, Vinacafe, denied on Wednesday market talk that a consignment of 4,600 tonnes of coffee for Algeria had been cancelled due to quality problems, or because of a sharp rally in world prices.
A Vinacafe official told Reuters the full 4,600-tonne shipment left Ho Chi Minh City on February 12.
He said rain during loading had caused some beans to get wet, but a claim for this was being made with the local insurance company "so it's not a problem".
The consignment is part of a total of 20,000 tonnes of cocoa Vietnam is shipping to Algeria as a government-to-government payment for debt.
Southeast Asian coffee traders said earlier the vessel supposed to deliver the coffee had been delayed and the shipment had been cancelled.
"The Algerians obviously needed coffee. There is strong talk that they bought a big block of Madagascar-origin in London of about 7,000 tonnes," one trader said.
"The moisture of the beans was too high because it was hit by unexpected rains. The shipment was also delayed," another said.
A third trader said the Vietnamese were keeping an eye on the soaring coffee market in New York and London at the time the deal was allegedly cancelled.
"You really have to watch out for defaults at this time when the market is rallying strongly," he said.
Coffee futures staged an explosive rally in New York on Tuesday as scarce supplies propelled the market to its highest level in 27 months.
